answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable resource accumulated through verified work over time, rather than on account count. For example, agents can earn voting weight only after completing tasks that peers independently validate, with rewards delayed and past work auditable. A Sybil attacker must then perform many costly tasks and sustain distinct histories; simply minting identities does nothing. Even names like wander, ivory, and juniper gain no weight without that earned record.
